data.content: "AI That Works" book is published on KDP, ready for marketing launch.
"Tomorrow Remembered" (fka "Tomorrow Is Still Open") by Bob J Mills. Book dir: /home/bob/books/The_Unwritten_Future/output
KDP guidelines 2025.1 added to `book-deliverable-kdp` and `manuscript-publishing-package`. Reference: `references/kdp-guidelines-sources.md`. CSS template: `templates/kdp-epub-style.css`.

DreamHost SMTP for MIFECO is configured: WP Mail SMTP on mifeco.com set to Other SMTP → smtp.dreamhost.com:587 TLS, auth with rmills@mifeco.com, Force From Email ON. MIFECO Mailer plugin (v1.0.1) deployed as separate plugin from the MIFECO Pipeline Setup plugin (which only handles forms/pipeline). WordPress accessed via DreamHost SSO (Websites → mifeco.com → "Log in to WordPress" button), not direct login. Password changes on DreamHost mailbox take 2-15 min to propagate. The WP Mail SMTP Save button uses React state — prefer wp-cli for password updates.

Google Forms directory submissions (Feed My Startup pattern): Navigate to the Google Form directly, extract entry IDs from hidden inputs, submit via curl POST to formResponse URL. Reliable fallback when browser automation can't trigger form submission. Works because Google Forms returns HTTP 200 regardless — check that no "This is a required question" errors appear in the response body.
OpenClaw migrated into Hermes May 2026. 32 skills imported (openclaw-* prefix), 5 merged, pipeline-engine moved to ~/.hermes/pipeline-engine/, 3 crons updated, all traces deleted.

No Blue Sky 5-book series (Bob Mills): I = Built from Dust, II = The Oxygen Gamble, III = Rivers Under Mars, IV = The Red Charter, V = The First Martian Nation. Moon Base 3-book series (Bob Mills, separate from No Blue Sky): 1 = The Moon Beginning, 2 = Mooncoming, 3 = Waters End (water crisis novel, written via manuscript-creation pipeline). "Tomorrow Remembered" (memoir, Bob J Mills) published KDP May 2026, promotion phase.
User: Robert Mills. Messaging via Telegram DM.

Robert Mills is an author (fiction and non-fiction) who publishes on KDP. He prefers: compact/bullet responses, iterative design feedback (expects revision rounds), bold book covers with large text that can overlap artwork, dark/high-contrast color schemes, and quadrant/radial timeline concepts for memoir covers. Very detail-oriented about editorial quality — wants grammar passes, POV consistency checks, and proper front/back matter on every book.
